title: Wichita Jazz Festival: Trombonist Nick Finzer with WSU Jazz Arts Ensemble I
cost: $30 / Students free with valid student ID
description: Location: Miller Concert Hall in the Duerksen Fine Arts Center. The Wichita Jazz Festival is proud to present internationally acclaimed trombonist Nick Finzer — hailed as a “Rising Star” in the DownBeat Critics Poll — live in concert alongside the incredible Wichita State University Jazz Arts 1 and the Mid-Kansas Jazz Band! Hailed as a “Rising Star” in the world of jazz (DownBeat Critics Poll), Nick Finzer is making waves in the music industry with his dynamic original compositions and trombone artistry. Finzer has toured the globe as a bandleader as well as sharing the stage with some of the most respected names in jazz. As both a headlining trombonist and an entrepreneur, Finzer is on a mission to spread the joy and power of jazz. In the past ten years, Finzer has released seven critically acclaimed albums, garnering features in the industry’s top publications and reaching the #1 position on the JazzWeek Radio charts. His original compositions have received national recognition through the honor of two ASCAP Young Jazz Composer Awards, and in 2020 he became a recipient of the prestigious New Jazz Works grant from Chamber Music America. Finzer’s album "Legacy” (2024) celebrated the centennial of trombone legend J.J. Johnson, reaching the top of the JazzWeek Radio Charts for three consecutive weeks. In 2018, Nick Finzer made history as the inaugural Professor of Jazz Trombone at the prestigious jazz program at the University of North Texas. As a leading figure in the world of jazz, Finzer brings a wealth of experience and expertise to both the university and the broader music community through his teaching, creative work, YouTube channel, and advisory roles with artists and institutions focused on long-term creative strategy and sustainability. Nick is an artist for Conn-Selmer Inc. and plays a King 3B+ Trombone. Get Tickets

title: ShiftSpace Gallery Opening Reception for 'Vox Nostra' Senior Showcase
description: Location: WSU ShiftSpace Gallery + Harvester Arts 120 E 1st St N, Wichita (inside The Lux at intersection of First and Market streets) Join us for the opening reception of Vox Nostra, a Senior Showcase featuring original work by graphic design and studio art students completing their Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in May 2026. From the students: This is the moment we step out of the classroom and into the workforce—not a quiet conclusion to our education but a bold new beginning. By claiming space through different mediums, perspectives, and processes, we present projects that are more than "art"; it is who we are and what we stand for. Some works may challenge expectations. Others may question systems, highlight overlooked issues, or amplify ideas that demand attention. Here we showcase that what we create is more than aesthetic output; it is perspective, position, and purpose made visible. See our work, understand our voices, and recognize us as emerging professionals who will shape our environments. It is not a demand for agreement—it is an invitation to engage. Vox Nostra is on view Friday, May 1–Friday, May 29, 2026. Exhibition and reception are free and open to all. Gallery hours: First Fridays: 6–8 p.m. Monday: 3–9 p.m. Tuesday–Friday: 3–6 p.m. Saturday: 10 a.m.–2 p.m.

title: Math for Everyone Lecture Series: 'Get in the Game - Data Analytics via Sports'
description: Location: Jabara Hall, Room 127 The last event in the "Math for Everyone Lecture Series" will be a double feature on April 30 and May 1. Part II : Title: Get in the Game: Data Analytics via Sports Time: 3 p.m., Friday, May 1 Location: Jabara Hall 127 Speaker: Professor Tim Chartier (Davidson College) Abstract: Sports analytics has gathered tremendous momentum as one of the most dynamic fields. Diving deep into the numbers of sports can be game changing or a framework for data analytics research. What questions can be explored? What actionable insights can be gleaned? From March Madness to national media broadcasts, analytics are becoming increasingly indispensable. Dr. Tim Chartier will discuss outlooks that help with successful analytics, and a variety of questions that can be tackled. He will also share how he leads students to dig into sports via data and their success across the NBA, MLB, NFL, NASCAR, ESPN and his own college teams. Following Friday's talk, please join us for an informal Q&A session with light refreshments. For more details about the Math for Everyone Lecture Series, please visit: https://sites.google.com/view/yuehjulin/event-and-outreach/math-for-everyone The lecture series is sponsored by NSF and by the Fairmount College of Liberal Arts and Sciences and the Department of Mathematics, Statistics, and Physics at Wichita State University.

title: ShiftSpace Gallery 'Vox Nostra' Senior Showcase exhibition
description: Location: WSU ShiftSpace Gallery + Harvester Arts 120 E 1st St N, Wichita (inside The Lux at intersection of First and Market streets) WSU’s School of Art, Design and Creative Industries present Vox Nostra, a Senior Showcase featuring original work by graphic design and studio art students completing their Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in May 2026. From the students: This is the moment we step out of the classroom and into the workforce—not a quiet conclusion to our education but a bold new beginning. By claiming space through different mediums, perspectives, and processes, we present projects that are more than “art”; it is who we are and what we stand for. Some works may challenge expectations. Others may question systems, highlight overlooked issues, or amplify ideas that demand attention. Here we showcase that what we create is more than aesthetic output; it is perspective, position, and purpose made visible. See our work, understand our voices, and recognize us as emerging professionals who will shape our environments. It is not a demand for agreement—it is an invitation to engage. Vox Nostra is on view Friday, May 1–Friday, May 29, 2026. Join us for an opening reception on First Friday, May 1, from 6–8 p.m. Exhibition and reception are free and open to all. Gallery hours: First Fridays: 6–8 p.m. Monday: 3–9 p.m. Tuesday–Friday: 3–6 p.m. Saturday: 10 a.m.–2 p.m.

title: Entrepreneur-in-Residence Keynote: 'The New Wave of Innovation'
description: Lauren Dunford will keynote at Wichita State on AI, robotics, manufacturing, and energy shaping the global economy and future innovation. As part of its Centennial celebration, the Barton School of Business welcomes Lauren Dunford — CEO and Co-Founder of Guidewheel and a global leader in AI-driven manufacturing — as Entrepreneur-in-Residence. Join us for a keynote exploring how artificial intelligence, robotics, and advanced manufacturing are transforming industries and redefining the future of energy. Dunford is a World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer and TED speaker whose company helps manufacturers worldwide boost productivity while reducing energy costs and emissions. Her work sits at the forefront of "physical AI," bringing intelligence to the machines that power the global economy. This forward-looking discussion will offer valuable insights for students, faculty, industry professionals, and anyone interested in how innovation is reshaping business and society. title: College of Education Centennial Open House
description: The Wichita State University College of Education will celebrate its centennial with a Centennial Open House on April 10–11, 2026, in Corbin Education Center. Alumni, students, faculty, staff and community partners are invited to return to campus to celebrate 100 years of the College of Education and its impact on education and communities across Kansas and beyond. Founded in 1926 with two professors and about two dozen students, the College of Education now serves over 2,000 students and provides unmatched applied learning opportunities.The centennial celebration provides an opportunity to reflect on the college’s history and impact while looking ahead to its next chapter. The event will include open houses in Corbin Education Center showcasing the college’s history, recognition at the Wichita State softball game on April 10 and centennial remarks and an alumni gathering on April 11. Join us as we celebrate a century of preparing educators, leaders and professionals and look ahead to the future of the College of Education. title: Guest Artist Recital - Wynona Wang, piano
description: Chinese pianist Wynona Wang has captured the attention of audiences around the world with a string of impressive competition successes, including winning the Bronze Medal at the 2024 Gina Bachauer International Artists Piano Competition, first prize at the 2018 Concert Artists Guild International Competition and 2017 Wideman International Piano Competition in Louisiana, and as a finalist and multi-prize winner in the 2023 Sydney International Piano Competition. Wynona has performed with many national and international symphonies, including the Sydney Symphony Orchestra, the Academic Symphony of the National Philharmonic Society of Ukraine, the Romanian Mihail Jora Philharmonic Orchestra, the Utah Symphony, the Pasadena Symphony, the Hilton Head Symphony, The Orchestra NOW, California North State Symphony, Midland Symphony, Roswell Symphony, and the Northwest Florida Symphony. Chamber music collaborations include Garrick Ohlsson, Gilbert Kalish, Joyce Yang, Inon Barnatan, Benjamin Beilman, Kristin Lee, Paul Neubauer, Ani Kavafian, Marcy Rosen, Andres Diaz, Sterling Elliott, and Jordan Bak. Born in Beijing, Wynona (Yinuo) began playing the piano at age 4 and studied at the Music Middle School of the Central Conservatory of Music in Beijing. In 2016, she was awarded a full scholarship to study at Southern Methodist University in Dallas, and in 2018, she earned her Performer’s Diploma under the tutelage of the eminent pianist Alessio Bax. She was awarded both the Paul Velucci Piano Award and the Harold Von Mickwitz Prize in Piano by SMU. Wynona earned her bachelor’s and master’s degrees at The Juilliard School, receiving the Arthur Rubinstein Commencement Award, and continues to pursue her Artist Diploma at Juilliard starting in Fall 2024 with Robert McDonald. Wynona Wang is a Young Steinway Artist. Wang will be performing solo piano works by Haydn, Schumann, Schulhoff, and Rachmaninoff.

title: WSU Jazz Invitational
description: The WSU Jazz Invitational is an annual celebration of jazz and jazz education, held every April in partnership with the Wichita Jazz Festival. This full-day event brings together student big bands from across the region for performances, adjudications, and educational clinics led by distinguished jazz educators. The invitational culminates in a headline concert featuring a renowned jazz artist performing with WSU’s Jazz Arts 1 Ensemble and the Mid-Kansas Jazz Ensemble, the region’s only auditioned high school honor jazz band. Event Highlights Student Performances – Middle school, high school, and collegiate big bands from across Kansas and surrounding states take the stage. Educational Clinics – Ensembles receive coaching from leading jazz educators and professional musicians. Headline Concert – A world-class jazz artist performs with WSU’s top jazz ensembles. Partnership with the Wichita Jazz Festival – The invitational serves as the Friday programming for this multi-day festival, which has brought jazz luminaries to Wichita for over 50 years. About the Wichita Jazz Festival Founded more than five decades ago, the Wichita Jazz Festival is one of the longest-running events of its kind in the country. Each year, the festival presents performances, workshops, and educational opportunities, keeping jazz thriving in the Wichita community. The WSU Jazz Invitational is one of the School of Music’s most visible events, bringing together students, educators, and artists to celebrate the power of jazz. For more information, please visit the festival's webpage.

title: 'Rat Bastard University: Home Sweet Home' Branden Lawless MFA thesis exhibition
description: Location: WSU ShiftSpace Gallery | Harvester Arts 120 E 1st St N, Wichita Branden Lawless presents his Master of Fine Arts thesis exhibition, Rat Bastard University: Home Sweet Home. Lawless is a ceramic sculptor and third-year MFA candidate at Wichita State University. He received his BFA from Kansas State University in 2021 and completed a post-baccalaureate program at Southeast Missouri State University in Cape Girardeau, Missouri. In 2019 he studied abroad at Lorenzo de’Medici in Florence, Italy, and later returned to a short-term residency at Studio Pescarella in Pietrasanta, Italy in 2023. Working primarily in ceramic sculpture, Lawless is the creator of Rat Bastard University, an ongoing satirical and immersive world that examines identity, love, power, and the absurdities of contemporary life. His practice ranges from large-scale figurative works to ceramic “action figures” and toy-inspired packaging that blur the boundaries between fine art and consumer culture. Through humor, exaggeration, and constructed narrative, his work invites viewers into a universe where contradiction, vulnerability, and rebellion coexist—positioning satire as both critique and self-reflection. Rat Bastard University: Home Sweet Home is on view Friday, April 3–Friday, April 24, 2026. Join us for an opening reception on First Friday, April 3, from 6–8 p.m. Gallery hours: First Fridays: 6–8 p.m. Monday: 3–9 p.m. Tuesday–Friday: 3–6 p.m. Saturday: 10 a.m.–2 p.m. The exhibition is a requirement of the MFA in Studio Art at Wichita State University.

title: Opening Reception 'Attention Icon' Madison Mullen MFA thesis exhibition
description: Location: WSU ShiftSpace Gallery | Harvester Arts 120 E 1st St N, Wichita Madison Mullen presents her Master of Fine Arts thesis exhibition, Attention Icon. Madison Mullen is an interdisciplinary artist based in Wichita, Kansas, working across painting, ceramics, video, and installation. Mullen’s practice explores the modern female experience, drawing on internet culture, advertising, and historical representations of the female form. Through a pop-surrealist visual language, she interrogates how media shapes behavior and identity by reassembling fragments of digital visual culture. Her work aims to reveal the contradictions between image and experience. Born and raised in Wichita, she is currently pursuing her Master of Fine Arts at Wichita State University. She has exhibited regionally and participated in artist residencies, including an international fellowship in Skopje, Macedonia. Attention Icon is on view Friday, April 3–Friday, April 24, 2026. Join us for an opening reception on First Friday, April 3, from 6–8 p.m. Gallery hours: First Fridays: 6–8 p.m. Monday: 3–9 p.m. Tuesday–Friday: 3–6 p.m. Saturday: 10 a.m.–2 p.m. The exhibition is a requirement of the MFA in Studio Art at Wichita State University.

title: Project Space Gallery Reception 'Building Futures: Printing Women'
description: Location: Project Space Gallery McKnight Art Center East (2nd floor) School of Art, Design and Creative Industries Reception: Friday, March 13 | 5–7 p.m. Exhibition on view through Friday, March 27 Gallery hours: Monday–Friday | 8 am.–5 p.m. Exhibition is free and open to all. Building Futures: Printing Women examines the history of print as a space of women's labor and agency. It considers what becomes visible when we approach the history of print through periodicals and newspapers led, owned, or circulated by women. The exhibition is part of an applied learning program in graphic design funded through the Kansas Applied Learning initiative. The project extends graphic design practice into interdisciplinary research by engaging students in archival investigation, historical analysis, independent publishing, and exhibition design. Three, research-based case studies across a range of time periods, geographies, and political contexts were assembled including: Women's Antifascist Front (AFŽ) of Yugoslavia, the British Women's Land Army, and a series of publications from the United States such as The Voice of Industry, The Una, The Woman's Advocate, and others. The exhibition presents work developed by students and faculty: Megan Ryan, Shelby DuVall, and Dr. Irma Puškarević.

title: Math for Everyone Lecture Series: 'Blown Away: What Knot to Do When Sailing'
description: Location: Jabara Hall, Room 127 The second talk in the Math for Everyone Lecture Series will take place at 3 p.m. on Friday, April 3. Our speaker will be Professor Colin Adams from Williams College. Title: Blown Away: What Knot to Do When Sailing by Sir Randolph Bacon III, cousin-in-law to Colin Adams Abstract: Being a tale of adventure on the high seas, involving great risk to the tale teller, and how an understanding of the mathematical theory of knots saved his bacon. No nautical or mathematical background assumed. About the speaker: Colin Adams is the Thomas T. Read Professor of mathematics at Williams College. He obtained his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin Madison in 1983. His work spans a number of areas of geometry and topology including the study of knots and hyperbolic 3-manifolds. In addition to his research work, Adams is known for his expository work. He has written a number of textbooks such as The Knot Book and most recently The Tiling Book. As a columnist for the Mathematical Intelligencer, he has written many interesting stories in his Mathematically Bent column, which have been collected into two books, Riot at the Calc Exam and Do Androids Dream of Symmetric Sheaves? Following the talk, there will be an informal Q&A session and light refreshments, providing for further discussion and engagement. For more details about the Math for Everyone Lecture Series, please visit: https://sites.google.com/view/yuehjulin/event-and-outreach/math-for-everyone The lecture series is sponsored by NSF and by the Fairmount College of Liberal Arts and Sciences and the Department of Mathematics, Statistics, and Physics at Wichita State University.

title: Open Streets ICT: WSU & Shocker Neighborhood

Connect with fellow community members, local vendors, organizations, and resources while enjoying a fun and active day outdoors. Leave your worries behind as we close off almost two miles of 17th Street from Oliver to Volutsia. This means no traffic, just open space for biking, walking, running, and so much more! Last April, more than 10,000 attendees filled 17th Street to celebrate Shocker Pride with us. Vendor and volunteer registration is now open! title: Campus Recreation Wellness Expo
description: Join us from 11:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. on Wednesday, March 4, as the Heskett Center transforms into a lively hub of health, learning, and fun. Alongside hundreds of fellow Shockers, you’ll discover new ways to boost your well‑being through interactive activities, medical screenings, and hands‑on wellness demos. title: 3rd Annual Health Research and Education Summit
description: To facilitate the collaboration between WSU, KU, and WSU Tech in the new Wichita Biomedical Campus, the WSU President’s Advisory Council (PIAC) has initiated an annual, one-day event for faculty to discuss interinstitutional research collaboration opportunities. This year, HealthHum is taking the lead with PIAC as co-sponsor. This year the roundtable will be separated into two parts. The morning session will focus on opportunities for research collaboration, and we are reaching out to community and industry partners to participate. The research scope will include a broad intersection of clinical work, the arts, humanities, applied studies and all the health-related work done. We will have short flash presentations on current research for our selected themes, followed by breakout discussions to allow members of the community to discuss ongoing and future research projects. The afternoon roundtable/brainstorming session will focus on educational collaboration opportunities like shared courses, guest lectures, course modules, or other ways to make our curricula richer or more efficient.

title: Clayton Staples Gallery: 'The Beginning Is the End Is the Beginning'
cost: Free and open to the public
description: Location: McKnight Art Center West, Clayton Staples Gallery "The Beginning Is the End Is the Beginning" Featuring original work by Joshua James Knott Gallery hours Monday-Friday, 8 a.m.-5 p.m. From the artist Art and life happen in fragments. I feel the creative act is an attempt to reconfigure those fragments. My studio practice is reliant on the act of collecting and accumulating an eclectic range of image resources. I modify and combine these appropriated fragments with my own drawings, collages, photographs, and other image-centric ephemera. This combination of personal mark-making and manipulated/appropriated source materials exemplifies a number of dualities, philosophically linked by their opposition, such as the abstract and the concrete, the digital and the analogue, the visceral and the ethereal, destruction and creation, chaos and order, and the sacred and the profane. The interplay of these contradictions is echoed throughout my work in various motifs and thematic variations, encouraging the viewer to make conceptual leaps between disparate works and generate individual connections. By balancing between and working through these qualities, my work speaks to an ongoing struggle to retain some vestige of hope while also acknowledging the vulnerability of the human condition. About the artist Knott holds a BFA in graphic design from Fort Hays State University; MFA from Tulane University; and an MFA in digital art and printmaking from Fort Hays State University. He is currently lead art instructor at Crowder College in Missouri. Exhibition-related events Exhibition-related events are free and open to the public. Artist Talk 4 p.m. on Thursday, March 12 in McKnight Art Center West, Room 210 Meet the Artist Reception 5 p.m. on Thursday, March 12 in McKnight Art Center West, Clayton Staples Gallery

description: Join us for WSU’s largest one day volunteer event! Join your fellow Shockers for a morning of volunteering throughout our community. Individuals, groups, organizations, students, staff and faculty are all invited to attend! Check-in for Wu's Big Event will be from 8:30 to 8:50 a.m. The kick-off will begin in the RSC Beggs Ballroom, located on the third floor of the Rhatigan Student Center at 9 a.m. with a light breakfast and kick-off celebration. description: Location: Ablah Library, Digital Scholars Commons Spreadsheets and data tables are tools to store and organize information collected from scholarly research, administrative projects, teaching, or class work. title: Love Data Week: Lay All Your Love on Metadata - A New API for Discovery
description: Location: Ablah Library, Digital Scholars Commons ICPSR maintains a collection of 60+ years of curated, richly described research data available for reuse by social science researchers at all levels of experience. A key challenge to disseminating this data is making it findable – helping users discover our data resources and making them aware of the ways in which ICPSR data can support their research needs. To address this challenge, ICPSR created a metadata export API (Application Programming Interface) that enables individuals and institutions to programmatically retrieve study-level metadata about ICPSR studies in multiple standards-based formats. The API supports reuse of ICPSR metadata in local catalogs, discovery systems, research workflows, and downstream applications. It extends and enriches ICPSR’s reach while increasing the FAIRness (findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability) of its data collections. In this presentation, members of ICPSR’s metadata team will demonstrate the new metadata export API and its benefits, including how to query it to find studies that meet specific research needs, what information is returned in the results, and how these exports improve upon ICPSR’s previous metadata distribution offerings. If you’re interested in incorporating ICPSR data into another discovery platform, this session will show you how to get started. Presenters: Mike Shallcross, Senior Associate Archivist, Metadata & Preservation, ICPSR Megan Chenoweth, Metadata Manager, Metadata & Preservation, ICPSR Jared Lyle, Archivist and Director, Metadata & Preservation, ICPSR Host Institution: ICPSR Note: We'll stream this webinar in the Digital Scholars Commons in Ablah Library. About Love Data Week Love Data Week is an international celebration of data, taking place every year during the week of Valentine’s Day. Universities, nonprofit organizations, government agencies, corporations and individuals are encouraged to host and participate in data-related events and activities.

title: Rie Bloomfield Organ Series: Lynne Davis, organ
cost: Free to all WSU students! ($6 - $12 otherwise)
description: The Rie Bloomfield Organ Series presents a recital by Lynne Davis at 7:30 p.m. Tuesday, March 24 in Wiedemann Hall on the Wichita State University campus. Internationally celebrated for her authority in French organ repertoire, Davis brings a career shaped by decades of study, performance and teaching in France and across Europe and North America. A prizewinner at the St. Albans International Organ Competition, she has performed in major cathedrals and concert halls throughout France and the United States and is a frequent performer, lecturer and juror for international organ competitions. Davis served for many years as a professor at leading French conservatories before returning to the U.S. to join the faculty at Wichita State University as the Robert L. Town Distinguished Professor of Organ. She is also the artistic director of the Rie Bloomfield Organ Series and Wednesdays in Wiedemann. This concert offers audiences the opportunity to hear one of the world’s leading interpreters of French organ music on WSU’s acclaimed Marcussen organ. Tickets are available through the College of Fine Arts Box Office at 316-978-3233 or online at wichita.edu/tickets.

title: Movies with Scientists: Fire of Love + Q&A with a Volcano Expert
description: Join us for a special movie night featuring the award-winning documentary Fire of Love, followed by a live Q&A led by WSU Geology Professor Dr. Melissa Scruggs. Fire of Love tells the extraordinary true story of Maurice and Katia Krafft, a fearless pair of volcanologists whose passion for understanding Earth’s most explosive phenomena led them on daring expeditions across the globe. Through stunning archival footage and a deeply human narrative, the film captures the beauty and danger of volcanoes. After the screening, stay for our Q&A with volcanologists who will share insights into volcanic activity, eruption forecasting, field research, and the science behind some of the dramatic events seen in the film. Whether you're a science enthusiast, a documentary lover, or simply curious about the explosive natural wonders of Earth, you'll find this screening event positively paroxysmal - and learn what that word means! This event is perfect for adults, students, science fans, film lovers, and the volcanically curious.

title: Watkins Visiting Professorship Lecture Series: Geology
description: Location: Hubbard Hall, Room 208 Geologic fieldwork as cutting-edge science: Recognition of new patterns leads to major advances. John Wakabayashi is a professor of geology at California State University, Fresno. During his applied geologic career, he worked on a variety of different projects in engineering and environmental geology, but also conducted and published research in varied aspects of tectonics and tectonic geomorphology. He also conducts research on long-time and length-scale geomorphology and linkages between surface processes and the clastic sedimentary record, including research on the topographic evolution of the Sierra Nevada. A common theme of all of his research is the application of mobile reference frames to better understand the essentially four-dimensional processes of tectonics and/or geomorphology. Intensive field work, including detailed geologic mapping and petrography are also foundational components of much of his work.

title: Artist Reception: Now & Then - Kate Van Steenhuyse
description: Location: McKnight Art Center, Clayton Staples Gallery This exhibition features new works by Kate Van Steenhuyse. "My paintings are mini playgrounds to practice discovery. I have always been fascinated by the relationships and systems (road maps, constellations, root systems, particle accelerator reactions, biodiversity, etc) which, layer upon overlapping layer, create our world. How do we make sense of this vastness enough to have any agency within it? Over the years, through my artistic exploration and professional endeavors, this interest has expanded from painting to nonprofit development and management, program and policy design, study of behavioral economics, arts-driven community development, and futures foresight strategies and facilitation."

title: Chris Buck - Artist Talk
description: The College of Fine Arts begins its 2025–26 Connoisseur Series with an extraordinary guest: acclaimed animator and director Chris Buck. Hosted by the School of Digital Arts, Buck will present an artist talk at 7 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 6, in the Shocker Studios lecture hall, 3803 E. Harry St., Suite 121, Wichita, KS 67218. The event will be followed by a student Q&A on Friday, Nov. 7. With nearly five decades in filmmaking, Buck is best known for directing Disney’s Frozen, Frozen II, Tarzan, and Wish, as well as Sony Pictures’ Surf’s Up. His work has earned him an Academy Award, BAFTA Award and Annie Award, cementing his place among the most celebrated storytellers in animation. The event is free and open to the public. Students and community members alike are invited to explore how imagination and collaboration bring beloved animated stories to life.

title: HPC Training Event: Learn to Harness High Performance Computing
description: Location: Online (Connection details will be sent after registration). Register using this Link: https://forms.office.com/r/vceYN1wWM1 Join us for a focused, hands-on introduction to High Performance Computing (HPC) designed for researchers, students, and professionals looking to accelerate their computational workflows. Featured Speaker: Dave Turner, Application Scientist at Kansas State University LinkedIn Profile: https://www.linkedin.com/in/dave-turner-64823336/ Dave brings years of experience supporting research computing across disciplines and will lead the discussion, offering practical insights and answering your questions. What is an Application Scientist? An Application Scientist is a technical expert who helps researchers make the most of HPC systems. They specialize in: Supporting scientific computing workflows Optimizing applications for performance and scalability Troubleshooting and training users Bridging the gap between research goals and computational resources Bonus Support Session: Dave will be available after the event to assist HPC users with questions, troubleshooting, and guidance on using BeoShock and other HPC resources. Bring your questions and get personalized help! What You’ll Learn: Basics of HPC systems and architecture How to access and run jobs on BeoShock HPC Tips for optimizing performance and managing resources Q&A with HPC experts Whether you're new to HPC or looking to sharpen your skills, this session will help you get started and make the most of available resources. Open to all disciplines – no prior HPC experience required! Send all questions to Terrance Figy, Associate Professor of Physics and Director of HPC (terrance.figy@wichita.edu).

title: Math for Everyone Lecture Series: How mathematics is making Hollywood movies better
description: Location: Jabara Hall, Room 127 Together with Robert Fraser, we are delighted to announce that the first talk in the Math for Everyone Lecture Series will take place at 3 p.m. on Friday, Nov. 14. Our speaker will be Professor Michael Dorff from Brigham Young University. Talk Information Title: How Mathematics Is Making Hollywood Movies Better? Abstract: What’s your favorite movie? Star Wars? Avatar? The Avengers? Frozen? What do these and all the highest-earning Hollywood movies since 2000 have in common? Mathematics! You probably didn’t think about it while watching these movies, but math was used to help make them. In this presentation, we will discuss how math is being used to create better and more realistic movies. Along the way, we will discuss some specific movies and the mathematics behind them. We will include examples from Disney’s 2013 movie Frozen (how to use math to create realistic-looking snow) to Pixar’s 2004 movie The Incredibles (how to use math to make an animated character move faster). Come and join us and get a better appreciation of mathematics and films. Following the talk, there will be an informal Q&A session and light refreshments, providing for further discussion and engagement. For more details about the Math for Everyone Lecture Series, please visit: https://sites.google.com/view/yuehjulin/event-and-outreach/math-for-everyone The lecture series is sponsored by NSF and by the Fairmount College of Liberal Arts and Sciences and the Department of Mathematics, Statistics, and Physics at Wichita State University.

title: Ulrich Museum + Tallgrass Film Festival present: 'Out of the Picture'
description: Location: Boulevard Old Town, 353 N. Mead St., Wichita, KS 67202 The Ulrich Museum is excited to serve as Community Partner for two screenings of "Out of the Picture" at Tallgrass Film Festival. This documentary film takes viewers inside the lives of some of the most relevant writers on art today, thinkers who are making sense of a period of unprecedented change to art and media. For more than a decade, the filmmakers turned their cameras on critics navigating these rapidly changing landscapes, including Carolina Miranda, formerly of the Los Angeles Times; Hrag Vartanian, of Hyperallergic; and Jeneé Osterheldt of The Boston Globe. “Out of the Picture” is poised to prompt a conversation about the nature of art, modern life, and how meaning gets made in the 21st century. As an Ulrich fan, you can save 30% on up to two tickets with discount code "community." Learn more and buy tickets in advance here.

title: Fairmount College Liberal Arts and Sciences Hall of Fame
description: We are pleased to announce our three 2026 Fairmount College of Liberal Arts and Sciences Hall of Fame honorees. Induction into the Fairmount College Hall of Fame is the highest recognition of outstanding alumni who have had a significant impact on the region, nation, and world. The induction ceremony will take place at 2 p.m., Feb. 3, 2026, in Wiedemann Hall. Warren E. Pickett 1969, BS-Physics and Mathematics; 1971, MS-Physics Pickett is a leading international expert in the field of high-temperature superconductors. He spent 18 years as a scientist at the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory before being hired by the University of California at Davis as a distinguished professor of physics. Robert E. Shields, 1968, BA-Political Science Shields built a solid career as one of the top litigators in the Southeast. Before retirement, he vigorously pursued cases against tobacco companies. He is considered an expert on hazardous waste and toxic torts. Scott W. Stucky, 1970, BA-History Stucky was appointed by former president George W. Bush in 2006 to serve on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces. He became chief judge of the body in August 2017, and, upon the expiration of his term of service in August 2021, was named senior judge.

We are pleased to announce our three 2026 Fairmount College of Liberal Arts and Sciences Hall of Fame honorees. Induction into the Fairmount College Hall of Fame is the highest recognition of outstanding alumni who have had a significant impact on the region, nation, and world. The induction ceremony will take place at 2 p.m., Feb. 3, 2026, in Wiedemann Hall. Warren E. Pickett 1969, BS-Physics and Mathematics; 1971, MS-Physics Pickett is a leading international expert in the field of high-temperature superconductors. He spent 18 years as a scientist at the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory before being hired by the University of California at Davis as a distinguished professor of physics. Robert E. Shields, 1968, BA-Political Science Shields built a solid career as one of the top litigators in the Southeast. Before retirement, he vigorously pursued cases against tobacco companies. He is considered an expert on hazardous waste and toxic torts. Scott W. Stucky, 1970, BA-History Stucky was appointed by former president George W. Bush in 2006 to serve on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces. He became chief judge of the body in August 2017, and, upon the expiration of his term of service in August 2021, was named senior judge.. This event is about Colleges and Schools, Fairmount College. It is Free.

title: Shocker Science Conversations: The Art and Physics of Flow Visualization
description: Location: Ulrich Art Museum, Dr. Sam and Jacque Kouri Collection Study Center Have you ever watched as cream mixes with your coffee? Stared into the flames of a fire? Seen how incense smoke streams upwards smoothly, then curls? Wondered why a candle flame is steady, then suddenly pulsates? Marveled at a thunderhead at sunset? Then you have participated in flow visualization. Literally, flow vis makes the physics of gases and liquids visible. Join Dr. Jean Hertzberg and enjoy learning about the aesthetics of flow visualization: beauty, power, destruction and the just plain weird things fluids can do. At the same time, explore the physics of a wide range of fluid dynamics. Refreshments start at 4:30 p.m., talk begins at 5 p.m.

title: Opera Theater presents: Opera Scenes and Songs
cost: Free to all WSU Students! ($6-$12 otherwise)
description: Wichita State University Opera Theater, under the direction of Professor Alan Held, will present the annual "Scenes and Songs" performance at 7:30 p.m. on Friday, Oct. 24, in Wiedemann Hall. "Scenes and Songs" has become one of the favorite performances on the yearly opera calendar since its inception in 2018. This year, the 60-minute performance features vignettes from multiple opera classics, including “The Tenderland”, “The Rake’s Progress”, “Mass”, “Trouble in Tahiti”, “A Little Night Music”, “Mefistofele”, and "Die Zauberflöte”. Experience the exceptional talent of Wichita State University Opera Theater, recognized as a leader in opera performance and education. Our productions feature outstanding individual instruction, fully staged operas with orchestra, and scene programs, often presented in the original language. Students develop their skills through a comprehensive curriculum that includes history, style, and acting classes, as well as master classes and performances throughout South Central Kansas. Join us for an engaging evening of operatic excellence, showcasing the future stars of the opera world. WSU Students can request their free student tickets in advance by going to the Fine Arts Box Office located in Duerksen Fine Arts Center during operating hours. Must show WSU student ID. Tickets can be purchased online through the Fine Arts Box Office or by phone at 316-978-3233.

title: WSU Opera Theater & ICT Repertory Theater Present: Amadeus
description: Shaffer’s 1979 masterpiece Amadeus dramatizes the rivalry between the boy-genius Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart and his contemporary, Court Composer Antonio Salieri. Told through Salieri’s eyes as the self-proclaimed “Patron Saint of Mediocrities,” the play unfolds as a gripping drama with elements of a thriller. Salieri’s jealousy of Mozart’s brilliance drives him into a tortured, obsessive struggle against both his rival and the God who chose to bestow genius on another. Performances run Oct. 10–19 at various times. Tickets are available through ICT Rep’s website. About the Playwright Sir Peter Shaffer (1926–2016) was a British playwright whose career spanned farce, drama and epic storytelling. His acclaimed works include Five-Finger Exercise (1960), Equus (1973), and Amadeus (1979), which won both critical and public praise and was later adapted into the Academy Award–winning 1984 film. Shaffer was knighted in 2001 for his contributions to theater. The performances will be held at: The Oliver Place 2512 N. Oliver Wichita, KS 67220

title: The Tenderland presented by WSU Opera Theater
description: Join us as Wichita State Opera Theater celebrates America’s 250th birthday with Aaron Copland’s heartfelt opera The Tender Land. Set in the rural Midwest, this poignant work tells the story of a farm family whose lives unfold against the backdrop of community, tradition, and the hope of new horizons. Inspired by Depression-era photographs and James Agee’s Let Us Now Praise Famous Men, Copland’s score blends sweeping lyricism with folk-inspired melodies, capturing both the quiet dignity and the restless spirit of rural America. With themes of family, love, and the passage of time, The Tender Land remains one of Copland’s most moving and accessible stage works. Performances will be held in Miller Concert Hall: Thursday, March 6, at 7:30 p.m. Sunday, March 8, at 3:00 p.m. Experience this American classic brought to life by WSU Opera Theater, with orchestra, in a production that honors Copland’s vision and the enduring beauty of the American heartland. WSU students can request their student ticket at no additional charge in advance by going to the Fine Arts Box Office in Duerksen Fine Arts Center during operating hours. Students must show their Shocker ID. Tickets can be purchased online through the Fine Arts Box Office or by phone at 316-978-3233.

description: Location: Woolsey Hall, Boettger Auditorium The W. Frank Barton School of Business at Wichita State University is thrilled to announce Maggie Topping as its Fall 2025 Executive-in-Residence. Topping, senior vice president, Human Resources & Communications at Textron Aviation, will bring her extensive expertise to enrich the school’s academic and professional environment. As Executive-in-Residence, Topping will participate in mentoring sessions, deliver guest lectures, and collaborate with Barton School leadership on program and curriculum innovations. She will also lead a keynote fireside chat titled "Driving Innovation Forward: Textron Aviation’s Balanced Approach to AI, Talent, and the Transformation of Work" alongside Luke Pankey, Chief Information Officer at Textron Aviation. RSVP at wichita.edu/executive-in-residence-keynote. The event is free and open to the public. Doors open at 9 a.m. About the Executive-in-Residence At Textron Aviation, Topping oversees human resources (HR), security, and corporate communications worldwide. Her responsibilities include global HR management, total rewards, organizational effectiveness, labor and employee relations, talent acquisition and development, employee safety, asset protection, media relations, employee communications, public affairs, and charitable giving and engagement. She has played a pivotal role in guiding Textron Aviation through major acquisitions, including the 2014 merger of Cessna Aircraft Company and Beechcraft Corporation and the 2015 acquisition of Able Engineering. Since joining Cessna Aircraft Company in 2001, Topping has advanced through roles including HR generalist and HR business leader, overseeing global HR operations and talent programs. Prior to Cessna, she worked at Honeywell Aerospace as an HR generalist and logistics manager. Topping holds a bachelor’s degree in Business Administration and Human Resources Management from Wichita State University, is a certified Textron Six Sigma Green Belt, and a graduate of the Textron Senior Executive Leadership Program. She actively serves on several boards, including Barton School’s Dean’s Advisory Board, WSU Tech, WSU Foundation & Alumni Engagement and WSU National Advisory Council. For more information about the Barton School, visit wichita.edu/business.

title: James Schwartz Distinguished Speaker Series: Michael Horn, Fall 2025 Keynote Speaker
description: The W. Frank Barton School of Business at Wichita State University is proud to announce Michael Horn as the keynote speaker for its Fall 2025 James Schwartz Distinguished Speaker Series. Horn is the author of several influential works, including the national bestseller Job Moves: 9 Steps for Making Progress in Your Career. His engaging and insightful presentation, "The New Career Playbook: Mastering Job Moves in a Changing World," will draw from his latest book to provide attendees with a fresh perspective on identifying their personal "quest for progress," evaluating opportunities, and taking ownership of their career paths. This free public event will be followed by a networking session. The first 75 attendees will receive a complimentary copy of Job Moves. For details and to RSVP, visit wichita.edu/new-career-playbook. About Michael Horn Horn is an acclaimed author and thought leader whose works include Disrupting Class: How Disruptive Innovation Will Change the Way the World Learns, Blended: Using Disruptive Innovation to Improve Schools, and Choosing College. He is the co-founder and a distinguished fellow at the Clayton Christensen Institute for Disruptive Innovation and teaches at the Harvard Graduate School of Education. In addition, he co-hosts two top-rated education podcasts — Future U and Class Disrupted — and is a regular contributor to Forbes.com. He also authors the Substack newsletter The Future of Education and serves as executive editor at Education Next. His work has been featured in leading outlets such as The New York Times, The Washington Post, The Atlantic, Harvard Business Review, and NBC.

title: Oratorio Concert
cost: Free to all WSU students! ($6 - $12 otherwise)
description: Featuring works by Linda Tutas Haugen, Johannes Brahms, and Craig Hella Johnson Join the Wichita State University choral ensembles and orchestra for an extraordinary evening of music that gives voice to resilience, compassion, and the enduring human spirit. This year’s Oratorio Concert brings together three deeply meaningful works that challenge performers artistically and invite audiences into stories of hope, struggle, and shared humanity. The program features Linda Tutas Haugen’s Anne Frank: A Living Voice, a powerful multimovement work that amplifies Anne Frank’s translated words through luminous choral writing. At once intimate and urgent, the piece allows singers and listeners to reflect on courage, identity, and the timeless relevance of Anne’s voice. Johannes Brahms’ Alto Rhapsody adds a contrasting Romantic depth to the program. This masterwork, scored for alto soloist, tenor-bass chorus, and orchestra, juxtaposes emotional isolation with the possibility of healing, offering the choir and orchestra a rich exploration of Brahms’ expressive and deeply human musical language. The choirs and orchestra will be joined in performance by Dr. Samantha Balboa, WSU Lecturer of Voice, who will be singing the memorable alto solo. The concert concludes with the choral suite from Craig Hella Johnson’s Considering Matthew Shepard, a genre-blending oratorio that weaves together poetic texts, folk elements, and contemporary choral writing to honor the life and legacy of Matthew Shepard. These movements invite performers and audiences to reflect on empathy, community, and the transformative power of compassion. Together, these works create an evening of music that not only showcases the artistry of WSU’s choirs and orchestra but also affirms the role of musical storytelling in illuminating the human experience. This is a program of remembrance, reflection, and hope—and one you won’t want to miss. Featured Ensembles: Concert Chorale Wu Choir Shocker Choir Symphony Orchestra Directors: Dr. Katelyn H. Peterson Dr. Ryan Beeken During operating hours, WSU students can present their Shocker Card and get a free ticket in advance at the Fine Arts Box Office in Duerksen Fine Arts Center. Tickets can be purchased online through the Fine Arts Box Office at https://wichita.edu/fineartsboxoffice or by phone at 316-978-3233. Please note: Online sales are suspended three hours before an event. The box office opens one hour before the event at the performance venue.

title: WSU Choirs Join Forces With the Wichita Symphony Orchestra for Verdi’s Requiem
description: This performance will take place at the Century II Performing Arts & Convention Center. Century II Performing Arts & Convention Center 225 W Douglas Ave Wichita, KS 67202 Experience the awe-inspiring power of Giuseppe Verdi’s Messa da requiem — a work of profound drama, spiritual depth, and musical grandeur. Composed in memory of the Italian poet Alessandro Manzoni, Verdi’s Requiem transcends the traditional liturgical form to deliver a deeply human meditation on life, death, and the hope for eternal peace. With operatic intensity, sweeping orchestration, and heart-stirring solos, the Requiem stands as one of the most compelling choral-orchestral masterpieces ever written. From the thunderous terror of the “Dies irae” to the serene beauty of the “Lacrimosa,” Verdi channels the full emotional spectrum in a work as theatrical as it is sacred. This special performance features the Wichita Symphony Chorus, Wichita State University Choirs, soprano Shannon Jennings, mezzo-soprano Christine Goerke, tenor Victor Starsky, and bass Raymond Aceto. Admission information is available at wichitasymphony.org.

title: WSU Choirs Join Forces With the Wichita Symphony Orchestra for Mozart’s Coronation
description: This performance will be held at the First United Methodist Church in downtown Wichita. Wichita First United Methodist Church 330 North Broadway Wichita, KS 67202 Experience the splendor of Mozart’s Mass in C Major, K.317 (“Coronation Mass”) in the resonant acoustics of First United Methodist Church. This special performance unites the Wichita Symphony Chorus, Wichita State University Choirs, Butler Community College Concert Choir, and the Wichita Community Children’s Choir under the direction of Dr. Ryan Beeken. Interwoven with Mozart’s luminous setting of the Ordinary of the Mass, the program offers a rich tapestry of sacred choral works through the ages, featuring diverse and expressive settings of the Propers by composers from across music history. From moments of intimate reflection to soaring passages of grandeur, this concert celebrates the enduring power of choral music to inspire and connect communities. Admission information is available at wichitasymphony.org.

title: Artist Talk: Abhidnya Ghuge
description: Location: McKnight Art Center, Room 210 Multidisciplinary artist Abhidnya Ghuge is known for her immersive site-responsive installations made of thousands of rolled woodblock prints. Her practice engages with themes of belonging and community and is inspired by the ephemeral nature of the human experience. These ideas are quite literally reflected in her means of creating through hands-on community collaboration, wherein different perspectives and patterns naturally emerge and enrich the piece. In connection with the site-specific installation she has been installing in the Polk/Wilson Gallery at the Ulrich Museum, Ghuge will share her unique practice, her story, and her inspirations. This free event starts at 6 p.m. on Tuesday, July 15 and takes place in McKnight Art Center, Room 210. Everyone is welcome!

title: DOD SBIR/STTR Proposal Preparation Webinar
description: Aug. 21, 2025 | 8:30 a.m. - 12:30 p.m. Do you want to submit a SBIR/STTR proposal to the Department of Defense (DOD), but don't know where to start? This webinar is for you! The DOD SBIR and STTR programs offer a wide range of opportunities for small firms to address military needs in just about every technology area from software to training systems, from medical products to air, land and sea platforms. In this webinar, you will receive a brief overview of DOD SBIR/STTR programs and learn about the recommended process for developing a Phase I SBIR/STTR proposal to the DOD, with attention paid to the differences among the various components and services. This event is hosted by Jim Greenwood. Registration is required. Registration Page: https://www.wichita.edu/research/WSUInitiatives/SBIR-STTR-Content/SBIR-STTR-Events.php

title: Workshop: USDA SBIR / STTR Seed, Launch, Grow
description: Curious about how to secure non-dilutive funding from the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) for your innovative research or ag-tech solution? Join us for a practical and informative workshop designed to demystify the USDA SBIR/STTR programs and help you develop a competitive proposal. Registration is open for the next Seed, Launch, Grow Workshop presented by the Great Plains SBIR Alliance! "Navigating USDA SBIR / STTR: A Beginner’s Guide for Startups, Small Businesses & Researchers" This session will cover: USDA SBIR/STTR eligibility and topic areas Key components of a successful proposal Common pitfalls and how to avoid them Who should attend: Entrepreneurs, researchers, and small business owners developing agricultural, environmental, or rural technologies University faculty or students interested in commercializing research Innovation ecosystem leaders supporting ag-based ventures Bonus Opportunity: Attendees will have the opportunity to meet directly with a USDA SBIR/STTR Program Manager following the workshop to discuss specific ideas and receive tailored guidance. The link to schedule a 15-minute one-one-one with the USDA Program Manager will be sent in the confirmation email once you register. Limited spots are available, if you do not see an open time slot from 2-3 p.m. CST for Tuesday, July 8, you will have the chance to schedule a call for a later date. Link to Register: https://lnkd.in/gwZwtGuW

title: Impulse Percussion Group - Gerald Scholl, conductor
cost: Free to all WSU students! ($6 - $12 otherwise)
description: Immerse yourself in the exhilarating world of percussion music with the Impulse Percussion Group (IPG) at Wichita State University! Serving as both a large percussion ensemble and a platform for smaller chamber ensembles, IPG welcomes auditions from majors and non-majors alike, fostering a diverse and inclusive musical community. Under the direction of Professor Jerry Scholl for over 15 years, the IPG has soared to new heights, achieving accolades such as winning second prize at the prestigious Wolff-Ilse Bing chamber music competition. With over ten premieres under their belt, including groundbreaking works like Paul Elwood’s "New Jerusalem for Percussion and Negro Spiritual Choir" and "Teppa and El Silencio," featuring maraca virtuoso Ed Harrison, IPG continually pushes the boundaries of percussion music. Renowned for their theatrical, contemporary, and thought-provoking performances, an IPG concert is not just a musical event—it's a sensory journey. Thanks to a strong partnership with WSU's media and stage crews, each IPG program is a seamless fusion of lights, sounds, and visuals, delivering an unforgettable experience for audiences. Don't miss your chance to witness the electrifying artistry of the Impulse Percussion Group—it's an experience like no other! During operating hours, WSU students can present their Shocker Card and get a free ticket in advance at the Fine Arts Box Office in Duerksen Fine Arts Center. Tickets can be purchased online through the Fine Arts Box Office at https://wichita.edu/fineartsboxoffice or by phone at 316-978-3233. Please note: Online sales are suspended three hours before an event. The box office opens one hour before the event at the performance venue.

title: Concert Chorale with WU & Shocker Choirs
cost: Free to all WSU students! ($6 - $12 otherwise)
description: Experience the exceptional artistry of the Wichita State University Concert Chorale, the premier choral ensemble at WSU. This highly selective, auditioned choir is open to all WSU students who seek a rigorous and quality choral experience, regardless of major. The Chorale cultivates an atmosphere of collegiality, fostering lasting memories and musical experiences through high artistic standards and the pursuit of excellence. The Concert Chorale performs a wide variety of repertoire from the Renaissance to the twenty-first century, ensuring a diverse and captivating program. Annually, they join other WSU choirs for the beloved Candlelight Christmas Concert and collaborate with the WSU Symphony Orchestra for the spring ‘Oratorio.’ Known for their excellence, the Chorale tours annually and is frequently invited to perform at prestigious professional conferences such as the American Choral Directors Association and the National Association for Music Education. Don’t miss this opportunity to witness the finest choral ensemble at WSU in a performance that promises to inspire and delight. Joining the Concert Chorale are Wichita State’s Wu Choir and Shocker Choir. The Wu Choir, a treble-voiced (soprano/alto) ensemble, and the Shocker Choir, a bass-voiced (tenor/bass) chorus, are comprised of music and non-music majors, reflecting their members’ diverse and inclusive musical interests. Open to singers campus-wide, these ensembles offer a quality choral experience through meaningful repertoire, collegiality, and excellent performance. Don’t miss this opportunity to enjoy the rich and dynamic choral traditions of WSU. During operating hours, WSU students can present their Shocker Card and get a free ticket in advance at the Fine Arts Box Office in Duerksen Fine Arts Center. title: 'Time Stands Still'
description: Time Stands Still by Pulitzer Prize-winner Donald Margulies is a riveting, deeply human drama set in a Brooklyn apartment, where photojournalist Sarah and her partner James, a foreign correspondent, attempt to heal and recalibrate after returning from the front lines of war. As they settle back into domestic life, their ideals, ambitions, and love for one another are quietly and powerfully tested. Margulies crafts a nuanced story about bearing witness to global suffering and the personal cost of stepping away. With sharp dialogue and emotional precision, Time Stands Still invites us to confront the tension between comfort and conscience, intimacy and independence, and what we owe to the world versus what we owe to ourselves. title: SPARK Spring Dance Concert
description: Space. Pulse. Art. Rhythm. Kinesis. Igniting the stage with energy, emotion, and movement, SPARK is a dynamic evening of dance that celebrates the elemental forces that drive human expression. Each piece in this electrifying repertoire explores a facet of the acronym that gives the concert its name — from the expansive freedom of space, to the visceral heartbeat of pulse, the transformative power of art, the driving beat of rhythm, and the ever-shifting force of kinesis. Featuring works by WSU dance faculty, local and regional choreographers, SPARK is a showcase of contemporary technique, innovative storytelling, and the boundless creativity of the human body in motion. Whether abstract or narrative, explosive or intimate, each performance ignites a dialogue between dancer and audience — a spark that lights the imagination. Join us for an unforgettable journey through the language of movement, where every step is a spark waiting to catch fire. Dates: February 26th - 28th, 2026 @ 7:30 P.M. / March 1st, 2026 @ 2:00 P.M. title: Bela Kiralyfalvi National Student Playwriting Competition Winner Staged Reading of 'Now We Are A Hundred'
description: The School of Performing Arts proudly presents a staged reading of the Bela Kiralyfalvi Nation Playwriting Competition winner Alaina Tennant's Now We Are A Hundred. Now We Are A Hundred, directed by Wichita State University alum Jane Gabbert, a poetic and emotionally rich historical drama set in post-WWII England. The story imagines a fictional reckoning between Christopher Robin Milne and his father, A.A. Milne—the creator of Winnie-the-Pooh. Through haunting dialogue and complex character dynamics, the play explores the emotional weight of literary fame, memory, and the search for personal identity amidst inherited legacy. title: Groundbreaking: Connected Nation Internet Exchange Point (IXP) Facility
description: Location: The event will be located directly across 21st Street from the WSU Eck Baseball Stadium. Join Connected Nation and Wichita State University at 3-4:30 p.m. on Thursday, May 15 for the first carrier-neutral Internet Exchange Point in the State of Kansas. This critical infrastructure — made possible by a $5 million grant from the State of Kansas — will enable higher performance, lower-latency connectivity regionally and pave the way for future technologies, including artificial intelligence. The event will begin with brief remarks from WSU President Dr. Richard Muma, elected officials, and project personnel, followed by the ceremonial groundbreaking. Parking Parking will be available in a designated area next to Eck Stadium. Refreshments will be provided.

title: Visiting Artist Talk | Justin Favela
description: Location: McKnight Art Center, Room 210 American mixed-media artist Justin Favela is known for large-scale installations and sculptures that are created in the style of piñatas. His work speaks to the intersection of American pop culture and his Guatemalan-Mexican heritage, and reflects his own experiences as a queer person of color in the U.S. Favela’s installations create immersive spaces that playfully dismantle institutional hierarchies, making his work just as subversive as it is accessible and fun. Favela will give an exciting artist talk associated with a new site-specific installation at the Ulrich, on view Fall 2025. Everyone is welcome at this free event!

title: Visiting Artist Talk | Abhidnya Ghuge
description: Location: McKnight Art Center, Room 210 Multidisciplinary artist Abhidnya Ghuge is known for her immersive site-responsive installations made of thousands of rolled woodblock prints. Her practice engages with themes of belonging and community and is inspired by the ephemeral nature of the human experience. These ideas are quite literally reflected in her means of creating through hands-on community collaboration, wherein different perspectives and patterns naturally emerge and enrich the piece. In connection with her Fall 2025 site-specific installation at the Ulrich, Ghuge will share her unique practice, her story, and her inspirations. Everyone is welcome at this free event!

title: Chi Alpha Campus Ministries
description: WE ARE A MOVEMENT OF COLLEGE-AGE MEN AND WOMEN EARNESTLY FOLLOWING JESUS. Our mission is to reconcile students to Christ, equipping them through spirit-filled communities of prayer, worship, fellowship, discipleship, and mission to transform the university, the marketplace, and the world. Chi Alpha is a group of students at Wichita State, which also exists on hundreds of other campuses across the nation and around the world. Chi Alpha may use Greek letters, but it is not a fraternity or a sorority. The Greek letters Chi and Alpha are the first letters of the Greek words for "Christ" and "Ambassador" respectively, so the name reveals a major purpose of Chi Alpha: to be Christ's ambassadors to the campus. In other words, Chi Alpha is a student group that wants to serve as a tangible reminder to fellow students that a God that you can't see loves and cares about you, even if you don't believe in Him. More than that, Chi Alpha is a Christian fellowship that provides a place for Christian students to grow in their faith and develop a stronger personal relationship with God. Chi Alpha is also a safe place for those that may be curious about Christianity to come and learn about Christ and the Bible. Everyone is welcome. Everyone can benefit. The idea behind Chi Alpha is not to be just another student organization, something that you write on your resume, but to be a place where lives are transformed for the better. Through Chi Alpha, close lifelong friendships develop. God has used Chi Alpha to work miracles in people's lives, to bring peace, healing, freedom from bondage, and to make broken lives new. Chi Alpha is an organization that welcomes all students from all over the world.

title: Panhellenic Council
description: The Panhellenic Council is the governing body and policy-making organization of the National Panhellenic Conference Sororities. The purpose of the Panhellenic Council is to coordinate the efforts of the individual sororities in matters of philanthropy, scholarship, leadership, and sisterhood. We are home to five out of the 26 sororities within the NPC: Alpha Phi, Delta Delta Delta, Delta Gamma, Gamma Phi Beta, and Kappa Kappa Gamma. The National Panhellenic Conference (NPC) is the umbrella organization for 26 (inter)national women's sororities throughout the United States and Canada. Founded in 1902, the NPC is the oldest and largest women's membership organization, representing more than 4 million women at over 650 college/university campuses and 4,600 local alumnae chapters in the United States and Canada. Each year, NPC sororities donate more than $5 million to philanthropic and charitable causes, donate over $2 million worth of scholarships to women, and volunteer over 500,000 hours of service to their communities.

To honor those who attain excellence in the study of the Spanish language and in the study of the literature and culture of the Spanish-speaking peoples; 2. To honor those who have made the Hispanic contributions to modern culture better known in the English-speaking world; 3. To encourage college and university students to acquire a greater interest in and a deeper understanding of Hispanic culture; 4. To foster friendly relations and mutual respect between the nations of Hispanic speech and those of English speech.

title: WSU Student Speech Language Hearing Association
description: The Wichita State University Student Speech-Language-Hearing Association (WSUSSLHA) is a student organization open to all WSU students. WSUSSLHA encourages professional interest among all students in the study of both normal and disordered human communication. It also provides a vehicle for student representation in matters of professional concern. WSUSSLHA is a local chapter of the National Student Speech-Language-Hearing Association (NSSLHA), a pre-professional organization for undergraduate and graduate students in speech language pathology and audiology. This organization promotes departmental and community involvement as well as opportunities for national membership and participation. NSSLHA is the student branch of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA), which is the national professional organization for this field. Social events sponsored by WSUSSLHA include the study parties and the Winter Holiday party. WSUSSLHA serves as a service organization by hosting guest speakers from non-profit organizations and donating both time and money to special events throughout the year.

title: Omega Psi Phi Fraternity, Inc
description: Epsilon Psi Undergraduate Chapter was formed with the purpose of joining young men with scholarly aspirations at Wichita State University in Wichita, Kansas. On February 1, 1968 this idea became a reality through the dedication and vision of the Chapter Founders after they submitted a letter to International Headquarters in October 1967. Founders: Bro. George Shaver, Bro. Wendell Smith, Bro. Hubert C. Hutcheson, Bro. Ewing Loftin, and Bro. Mayhugh Sneed. Since then, Epsilon Psi has continued to provide an opportunity for young men to be productive in at the college level and in the greater Wichita area. Many brothers from Epsilon Psi have graduated and transitioned to Gamma Upsilon and even chartered a second graduate chapter, Mu Nu Nu, thereby allowing Omega to have that much more influence in community for many years. Brothers are educationally equipped and have gone on to be many things; lawyers, law enforcement officers, doctors, teachers, military officers, and much more. Many are well known not only in Wichita, but across the Midwest and the United States Epsilon Psi provides the young college men the foundation to do well with the Cardinal Principles of Manhood, Scholarship, Perseverance, and Uplift. With these principles as underpinnings, it makes it easy for them to perform "Service" on and off campus.

title: Shocker Organization for LGBTQIA+ Advocacy & Research
description: Purposes The purpose of SOLAR would include three main components: Researching, educating, and advocating. Researching and educating would be very closely involved with advocating, being somewhat distinct. Research: SOLAR would research the impacts of certain policies and legislation, how to combat oppressive legislature and government, the logistics of government, the process of resolutions becoming law, alternate policy solutions, and much more. The research aspect of SOLAR would be academic research. Research would likely be done individually in preparation for a protest or to teach others about a particular topic. Educate: SOLAR would then take this information and convey it as best we can to the student population at WSU. While we want students to join SOLAR, we want to intentionally share information with as many people as possible. Educating could look like creating resources to combat oppressive legislation, tools to navigate the difficulties of being a part of the LGBTQ+ community right now. Writing informative essays or speaking out on certain societal issues on or around campus and generally using your knowledge and sharing it to benefit the queer and trans community in any way you can. Advocate: Advocating and protesting would be a unique function of SOLAR. The main form of advocating would be peaceful protesting on campus. WSU is supportive of freedom of expression (see details here) and should be a right utilized to its full extent. College campus protests often gain lots of media attention and offer to amplify our voices to ensure queer and trans youth voices are heard. Advocating doesn’t have to look like protesting, though. I would also love to create a significant social media presence for SOLAR to reach beyond just WSU. Public speaking opportunities are also a great way to advocate. Goals SOLAR’s broad goals are essentially the purposes above; however, I have a few specific goals for SOLAR. Policy Influence: I believe it’s incredibly important for us as college students and young adults to understand that our voices are very influential. Our long-term goal for SOLAR is to influence policies on WSU’s campus and in the greater Wichita area. Amplify Voices: Develop and use our platform to amplify not only queer and trans voices, but also other minorities. The goal is to create a clear and accessible platform for college students to be able to use their voice to inspire change. Form Connections: Leveraging connections is essential for SOLAR to be as effective and influential as possible. Forming and maintaining relationships with other student organizations on campus will be a crucial aspect of growing SOLAR’s general body. There is an inherent connection with Spectrum, due to the fact that SOLAR would be an organization under Spectrum. Forming a connection with SGA will be critical to ensuring that queer and trans perspectives are taken into account when making important decisions that impact students. Another long term goal I have is to become a supplemental organization to the ACLU in Kansas. Additionally, there’s a distinct opportunity to leverage connections in the political science department in the local Kansas government to further ensure queer and trans voices are heard. Beacon of Hope: A goal that I have for SOLAR that is a lot more nebulous and hard to measure is being a beacon of hope for queer and trans youth. It’s very easy to become discouraged and feel hopeless because of the sheer amount of legislation targeting queer and trans individuals. I want SOLAR to be a beacon of hope for young trans and queer individuals to remind us that we aren’t defenseless in the fight for our rights and that we’re not alone. Meeting Plans & Ideas SOLAR would meet twice a month and would follow two general meeting formats. Informational Meetings: Informational meetings would likely be the majority of SOLAR’s meetings, especially at first. These meetings would include the basics of advocacy and protesting, developing research skills, how legislation is passed, etc., that will be helpful information for members of SOLAR to know as well as the general student body. Protesting: Protesting meetings would be the main focus of SOLAR and our goal would be to participate in a protest 3 times per semester. Since I’m inexperienced in organizing protests (and presumably so are all of you) I have no concept of how reasonable of a goal this is and could very well change. Protesting would be likely limited to WSU’s campus to gain enough recognition in the Wichita area to assist and participate in larger protests in the community. For now, the plan is to remain on campus though. There would also likely be meetings used to prepare for protests.

Forming and maintaining relationships with other student organizations on campus will be a crucial aspect of growing SOLAR’s general body. There is an inherent connection with Spectrum, due to the fact that SOLAR would be an organization under Spectrum. Forming a connection with SGA will be critical to ensuring that queer and trans perspectives are taken into account when making important decisions that impact students. Another long term goal I have is to become a supplemental organization to the ACLU in Kansas. Additionally, there’s a distinct opportunity to leverage connections in the political science department in the local Kansas government to further ensure queer and trans voices are heard. Beacon of Hope: A goal that I have for SOLAR that is a lot more nebulous and hard to measure is being a beacon of hope for queer and trans youth. It’s very easy to become discouraged and feel hopeless because of the sheer amount of legislation targeting queer and trans individuals. I want SOLAR to be a beacon of hope for young trans and queer individuals to remind us that we aren’t defenseless in the fight for our rights and that we’re not alone. Meeting Plans & Ideas SOLAR would meet twice a month and would follow two general meeting formats. Informational Meetings: Informational meetings would likely be the majority of SOLAR’s meetings, especially at first. These meetings would include the basics of advocacy and protesting, developing research skills, how legislation is passed, etc., that will be helpful information for members of SOLAR to know as well as the general student body. Protesting: Protesting meetings would be the main focus of SOLAR and our goal would be to participate in a protest 3 times per semester. Since I’m inexperienced in organizing protests (and presumably so are all of you) I have no concept of how reasonable of a goal this is and could very well change. Protesting would be likely limited to WSU’s campus to gain enough recognition in the Wichita area to assist and participate in larger protests in the community. For now, the plan is to remain on campus though. There would also likely be meetings used to prepare for protests.. More info: https://wichita.campuslabs.com/engage/organization/solar

title: International Women of Color
description: Since arriving at WSU, I have been searching for a community that encompasses the intersectionality of feminism and what it entails to be an international woman of color. While on the search, I came across a gap, a lack of diversity, and representation in most of the organizations that I talked to on campus, especially those addressing the difficulty of moving to America or advocates for those who do. This organization will recognize the unique struggles that international women of color may face in their long journey. Our organization will do its best to provide a safe space for those who are having a hard time with relocation and those who don’t feel a sense of belonging. Because this community is not just about surviving, but it is about living and embracing life. Through our organization we are not only putting effort in making others feel welcome and connected, but we will also try to make each and every member seen, heard, and supported.

title: Hispanic American Leadership Organization
description: The Hispanic American Leadership Organization (HALO) at Wichita State University empowers Hispanic and Latine students through academic support, cultural celebration, and leadership development. As a campus agency, HALO fosters a strong sense of belonging, promotes student success, and champions inclusive excellence across the university. HALO’s mission is to educate, empower, and develop future leaders by providing opportunities for personal growth, academic achievement, and professional advancement. Its core values—Inclusivity, Cultural Empowerment, Leadership Development, Community Engagement, Academic Success, and Collaboration—guide every initiative. HALO serves as the agency home for six registered student organizations that represent the diversity and leadership within the Hispanic and Latine community at Wichita State. These include: Kappa Delta Chi Sorority, Inc. Omega Delta Phi Fraternity, Inc. Sigma Lambda Beta International Fraternity, Inc. SHPE: Leading Hispanics in STEM Paraguayan Student Association Corazón Latina Each organization contributes to HALO’s mission through service, cultural engagement, and academic excellence. Throughout the year, HALO hosts high-impact programming, including leadership workshops, cultural heritage celebrations, guest speakers, and two annual spring conferences centered on empowerment, education, and access to resources. These events foster intercultural dialogue and deepen cultural awareness on campus. Beyond the classroom, HALO supports student success through mentorship, resume building, networking events, and alumni panels. It also partners with local organizations, offers volunteer opportunities, and awards scholarships to high school students—helping reduce barriers to higher education for Latine youth in Wichita. For many, HALO becomes a “home away from home,” offering community, cultural pride, and the tools to lead. Through advocacy, collaboration, and student-centered programming, HALO strengthens campus life and uplifts historically underrepresented voices at Wichita State.

title: Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc.
description: *Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc* 10 astute men attending Indiana University at Bloomington saw their vision come to fruition on the 5th day of January, 1911. The fraternity has never limited membership based on color, creed or national origin. Since its arrival on campus 64 years ago, Delta Upsilon has been a staple of multicultural greek life on the campus of WSU. Delta Upsilon has the pleasure of being mentored by one of the strongest Alumni chapters in the nation, the Wichita Alumni chapter of Kappa Alpha Psi; which houses some of the top Lawyers, Doctors, and Businessmen in the area.
