title: The Satanic Temple Club
description: The purpose of The Satanic Temple Club is to follow the fundamental seven tenets: One should strive to act with compassion and empathy toward all creatures in accordance with reason. The struggle for justice is an ongoing and necessary pursuit that should prevail over laws and institutions. One’s own body is inviolable, subject to one’s own will alone. The freedoms of others should be respected, including the freedom to offend. To willfully and unjustly encroach on the freedoms of another is to forgo one’s own. Beliefs should conform to one’s best scientific understanding of the world. One should take care never to distort scientific facts to fit one’s beliefs. People are fallible. If one makes a mistake, one should do one’s best to rectify it and resolve any harm that might have been caused. Every tenant is a guiding principle designed to inspire nobility in action and thought. The spirit of compassion, wisdom, and justice should always prevail over the written or spoken word.

title: The Cosplay Club
description: The Cosplay Club is a vibrant and inclusive community that celebrates the art of cosplay, where members come together to express their passion for dressing up as their favorite characters from various genres, including anime, manga, comics, movies, and video games. The club provides a creative and welcoming space for individuals of all skill levels and interests in the world of cosplay. Activities within "The Cosplay Club" range from regular meet-ups and workshops to share crafting techniques, costume design tips, and makeup tutorials. Members have the opportunity to showcase their cosplay creations, participate in themed photo shoots, and collaborate on group projects. The club also hosts cosplay contests and events, fostering friendly competition and encouraging members to showcase their unique interpretations of beloved characters. In addition to local events, "The Cosplay Club" organizes group outings to conventions, creating opportunities for members to immerse themselves in the larger cosplay community. Whether it's attending anime, comic, or gaming conventions, members of the club can experience the excitement of larger-scale gatherings, participate in meet-ups with fellow enthusiasts, and showcase their creative talents on a broader stage. It's a space where creativity knows no bounds, and everyone is encouraged to express their love for cosplay in a supportive and inclusive community that extends beyond regular club activities.

description: Wichita State University SHARE of Planned Parenthood is an inclusive student-based organization at Wichita State University comprised of undergraduate, graduate students, and community members. title: Phi Alpha Honor Society
description: The concept of a national social work honor society came from a group of undergraduate social work students at Michigan State University in 1960. Investigation revealed that local chapters existed at three schools. Those three schools, along with a few other schools, formed a National Honor Society Committee in November 1960. For more than a year, this committee worked on the constitution and other administrative matters. The name Phi Alpha and the key were adopted from the local chapter which existed at Florida State University. The constitution and formal organization were completed in 1962, and six chapters qualified to become "charter chapters." They were: Florida State University, Michigan State University, Ohio Northern University, Central State College, University of Dayton and the University of Tennessee. Over 110 chapters currently exist, and the addition of new chapters continues.

title: Delta Upsilon - Wichita Webster Chapter
description: Delta Upsilon was founded in 1834 and follows the belief that a fraternity should have a foundation built upon brotherhood, not secrecy. Over one-hundred and fifty years later, Delta Upsilon continues to follow this ideal and is dedicated to Building Better Men. We take pride that there is no secret handshake, that initiation is open to anyone, and we are a non-hazing fraternity. Delta Upsilon is focused around four main principles: friendship, character, culture, and justice. It is through these four principles that guide our members to excel not only in college, but throughout their entire lives. We are the largest and oldest North American non-secret fraternity and the sixth-oldest general fraternity. Your experience with Wichita Webster Chapter of Delta Upsilon will provide you with both challenges and great opportunities

Where do you meet? Rhatigan Student Center Our meetings move around, but you can find the specific locations under Events, on our Facebook page, or on our Instagram page. Who can come? Everyone! Whether you identify as Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans, Questioning, Queer, Asexual, Straight, or anything in between, you are welcome! Both enrolled students and members of the community who aren't enrolled are welcome. What's our purpose? We envision a campus that promotes lifelong success for people of all sexualities and gender identities. We work toward this vision by sustaining a visible, active, inclusive, and fun community that promotes academic success, fosters social and professional connections, and serves as a strong voice for LGBTQ+ students.

title: Student Health Services
description: The mission of Student Health Services at Wichita State University is to assist students in maintaining a state of optimum physical and mental wellness. Our professionals provide medical treatment for ill or injured students, and offer guidance and education in health matters to promote good health and prevent disease. Services include diagnosis and treatment of illnesses, over-the-counter and prescription medications and a variety of vaccinations and immunizations. Our professional staff is comprised of registered nurses, registered nurse practitioners, physicians, a registered pharmacist and a dietitian. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x6y-Qb1-KwY&t=110s

title: Student Activities Council
description: SAC is a student-led organization that hosts exciting, engaging, and thought-provoking events and programs. We are always looking for Shockers with an interest in creating memorable experiences, learning new skills, and having fun! Members serve on of the following SAC committees to plan, market, and implement dozens of events and experiences each year. Arts & Culture Committee The Arts & Culture Committee hosts events and experiences that explore music, performing arts, literature, film, and more. Members plan annual events like the Maker Market, Road Trips, and plan new programs each semester. Digital Content TeamOur Digital Content Team and is responsible for the promotion of SAC programs and initiatives through the creation of social media campaigns, video content, and drive the online presence of the SAC brand. Shocker Night LifeSNL hosts live entertainment and evening events like hypnotists, casino night, comedians, and more. Members engage with artists, promote events, and create an inviting environment for attendees. Annual programs include dance parties, movie experiences, casino night, and entertainers. Special Events CommitteeThe Special Events Committee plans programs intended for Shockers with children and/or siblings, our Veteran/Military students, and daytime programs for commuters. Annual events include Trunk or Treat, Big Bingo, and Fairmount Formal. View Our Committee Meeting Times What do members do? Serve on a committee to plan, promote, and execute events Attend SAC Member Retreats, held once each semester Participate in optional socials, workshops, and committee functions Gain essential career skills in critical thinking, decision making, planning, organizing, and communication Make lifelong friendships! How do I join a committee? Complete our Member Interest Form and get connected or drop by a committee meeting that meet's your schedule. Our chairpersons will meet with you to discuss member requirements, responsibilities, and benefits. Check out the events section for all committee times and locations. Be a part of Shaping the Shocker Experience!

title: Hispanics In Healthcare
description: Hispanics in Healthcare (HIH) isn’t just an organization; it’s a movement dedicated to empowering the next generation of Hispanic healthcare professionals. We exist to uplift and support Hispanic students who are boldly pursuing careers in the medical field, ensuring they have the resources, representation, and advocacy to make a lasting impact on our communities. Our mission is to bridge the gap in healthcare disparities by equipping students with the necessary tools to succeed. From shadowing experiences and community service opportunities to medical Spanish interpreting workshops, we provide a strong foundation for both professional and personal growth. Through these initiatives, we foster a vibrant, close-knit community, one built on connection, collaboration, and a shared vision for the future. HIH is more than just opportunity, it’s inspiration. We recognize the struggles, sacrifices, and resilience of Hispanic students in healthcare. Here, we celebrate our heritage, embrace our differences, and lift each other up. We are a force for change, striving to break barriers, amplify voices, and increase Hispanic representation in Medicine. Together, we are not just pursuing careers, we are shaping the future of Hispanic healthcare.

title: Wichita State University Wakeboard & Water Ski Club
description: Students will learn the ropes of 3-event water skiing by joining the team. Practices will take place during the spring, summer, and fall at Mystic Lakes in Maize, KS. Take advantage of this exciting opportunity to be coached by local water ski professionals, and develop your skills on the water. Skiers may choose to participate in any or all 3 events that include slalom, trick, and jump. Limited equipment will be provided. Familiarizing yourself with the scoring system for each event will better position you and the team to compete against collegiate skiers across the midwest. This is a coed sport where wakeboarding and kneeboarding is welcomed.

description: The Alpha Theta Chapter of Sigma Psi Zeta Sorority, Inc. at Wichita State University, was formally established on November 16, 2013. Sigma Psi Zeta is a progressive, multicultural Greek Organization that provides a means to success and support for womxn, particularly womxn of color. The sorority builds on the unity of strong and independent leaders to affect change in our organization, our campuses, and our local communities. We are a cultural, social, educational, and community service-oriented sorority, as well as the first Greek-lettered sorority of its kind to be established on the East Coast. in addition, we are one of the largest historically in Asian Pacific Islander Desi American (APIDA) Greek organizations and a founding member of the National APIDA Panhellenic Association (NAPA). We strive to create a network for strong, ambitious womxn and promote professional, educational, and individual development. Sigma Psi Zeta is an official partner of It's On Us, the White House Initiative to end sexual assault on college campuses. We aim to be a community of pioneers and innovators offering opportunities to develop professional and interpersonal skills in service of education, cultural awareness, and our national philanthropy. For additional information, check out our website or contact the Chapter President, Amy Nguyen, at syz.akiriko@gmail.com

title: Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc.
description: Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc. was founded on Tuesday December 4th, 1906 on the campus of Cornell University in Ithaca, New York. Initially a literary society meant to serve as a study and support group for minority students who faced racial prejudice, both educationally and socially, at Cornell. The literary society developed into a fraternity founded by seven college men who recognized the need for a strong bond of brotherhood among African descendants in this country. The fraternity's seven founders and early leaders succeeded to build a strong foundation for the organization's mission to develop leaders, promote brotherhood and academic excellence, while providing service and advocacy for our communities. The fraternity's mission continues to push brothers of Alpha Phi Alpha to help correct the educational, economic, political, and social injustices faced by African Americans. Alpha Phi Alpha has long stood at the forefront of the African-American community's fight for civil rights through leaders such as W.E.B. DuBois, Adam Clayton Powell, Jr., Edward Brooke, Martin Luther King, Jr., Thurgood Marshall, Andrew Young, William Gray, Paul Robeson, and many others. The Delta Mu chapter of Alpha Phi Alpha was founded on March 25th, 1950 by 9 distinctive men on the campus of Wichita State University. The Delta Mu chapter hosts annual events on campus such as the Miss Black and Gold Scholarship Pageant, Stroll Like an Alpha, SNAPS Open Mic Nights, and voter registration drives. The brothers on campus continues to push the fraternity's four national programs known as A Voteless People is a Hopeless People, Project Alpha, My Brother's Keeper, and Go-to-High-School, Go-to-College. All of which help realize the fraternity's vision of to stimulate the ambition of its members; to prepare them for the greatest usefulness in the causes of humanity, freedom, and dignity of the individual; to encourage the highest and noblest form of manhood; and to aid downtrodden humanity in its efforts to achieve higher social, economic and intellectual status.

title: Shocker Racing: Baja SAE
description: Baja SAE is an international collegiate design competition sponsored by the Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE). The contest challenges each team to function as a small manufacturing firm whose task is to design, fabricate, market, and race an off-road vehicle prototype that will be evaluated from a variety of manufacturing angles. Each year, various SAE sections host three competitions in which teams from across the nation and around the world bring their vehicles to undergo rigorous testing. The vehicles are judged based on their ability to traverse a harsh, off-road racing course, while not succumbing to the rigors of it. WSU’s Baja SAE Team, Shocker Racing, was started in 1986, and the first year to compete was 1993. Since then, Shocker Racing has competed in on average two competitions annually.

title: Indian Student Association
description: The Indian Students Association (ISA) is one of the largest and most dynamic student organizations on campus at the Wichita State University (WSU). The organization is recognized and partly funded by the Student Government Association (SGA). An Indian student community of more than 400 and guiding faculty make it one of the most active student bodies at WSU. True to the culture of India, the organization is house to a myriad of cultural habits, traditions, costumes, religions, languages, and dialects spread across the length and breadth of India. In an effort to familiarize the west with the fascinatingly diverse and cultural colors of India, the ISA organizes Vasanth and India Nite every year, two colorful nights filled with entertainment and extravagance at their best. ISA has always been and will continue to be at the forefront in networking with different organizations on campus and in times of need of students be they Indian or otherwise. ISA is proud to contribute its part toward 'Shocker Pride.'

title: International Business Studies Association
description: IBSA, The International Business Studies Association, is a non-profit student-run organization that is made up of highly motivated students from diverse backgrounds who are globally minded and conscientious. IBSA is committed to instilling cultural intelligence, professional acumen, and other "soft skills" to our student body through community service, educational programs, and interaction with the local export-oriented business community. All MAJORS are WELCOME! IBSA works closely with WSU's Center for International Business Advancement by coordinating the World Trade Council of Wichita’s monthly meetings (which are free of charge to IBSA members). These meetings provide student members with unparalleled insight and contact with Executives and Captains of Industry from the International business community. Past meetings have featured Hong Kong’s trade Commissioner to the United States, the Consular General of India, the Ambassador From Iraq to the United States, and Senator Bob Dole.

Our sisterhood stretches across the United States and Canada with 175 collegiate campuses, 131 alumnae communities, and a community of more than 250,000 members committed to lifelong friendships, leadership, academic excellence, personal growth and community involvement. Alpha Phi offers a unique bond of sisterhood, a spirit of generosity, high expectations for character and a drive for innovation. These are our High Ideals of Membership, which define what it truly means to be an Alpha Phi. The objectives of our Fraternity are the promotion of growth in character, unity of feeling, sisterly affection and social communion among our members. We live by our motto: Union Hand in Hand.

title: SHPE: Leading Hispanics in STEM
description: SHPE (Leading Hispanics in Stem) envisions a future where Hispanics are influential leaders in STEM fields. Rooted in our values of familia, service, resilience, and education, we strive to empower our community by providing resources, support, and opportunities for growth. On campus, we hold biweekly meetings that range from social events to foster the familia aspect, to resume-building workshops that promote educational excellence, and guest speaker sessions that facilitate networking opportunities. We also believe in giving back to our community by inspiring local youth to pursue STEM careers. Each year, our members have the chance to attend the SHPE National Convention, the largest gathering of Hispanic STEM students, offering unparalleled networking, professional development, and internship opportunities. Through these initiatives, we are committed to helping Hispanics realize their full potential and make a significant impact in the STEM world. Join us and be part of a transformative journey.

title: Chi Sigma Tau National Fraternity, Inc.
description: Chi Sigma Tau National Fraternity, Incorporated is the first Asian American Interest fraternity to have been founded in the Midwest on September 9, 1999. We establish lifelong brotherhood, develop leadership skills, institute a mentor program for the younger members, promote Asian awareness by bringing a voice to the Asian American community on campus, and work to expand our unique style of brotherhood to other campuses. Although we were founded as an Asian Interest Fraternity, Chi Sigma Tau is non-exclusive and openly welcomes potential members from all walks of life. We are all like-minded people and strive to achieve the same goals: graduate, expand the fraternity, and develop our leadership capabilities - in essence, to become better rounded men with honor, integrity and selflessness. We have a strict non-hazing policy and therefore will not conspire to engage in or commit any act which endangers the health or safety of a person, or subject him or her to onerous, degrading or hazardous tasks, for the purpose of admission into, or affiliation with our Organization. Said acts are considered hazing regardless of an individual’s willingness to participate in the activity. This organization is in accordance with all university policies regarding hazing, including the Wichita State University Student Code of Conduct and the Kansas Hazing Law Statute 21-3434. The Epsilon Chapter of Chi Sigma Tau National Fraternity, Inc. was established on December 5th, 2009 at Wichita State University.
